text:
omar: Hey team — saw a sharp p99 tail during the long-context perf run on prod tonight. Investigating kernel choice + KV behavior. Anyone oncall?
ben: I'm looking. Which routes? longchat-infer and rerank-heavy?
sangeeta: primarily longchat-infer (ctx ~6k tokens) and batch-embed for very long docs. p95 is fine, p99 jumps ~3x.
omar: attaching quick profiler excerpt (copied):

```
profile: endpoint=longchat-infer
top_ops:
  - kv_lookup: 42% (serial stalls when cache miss)
  - softmax_kernel: 18%
  - attn_matmul: 14%
  - cuda_sync: 9% (blocking on tail microbatch)
microbatch_stats:
  median_size: 3
  p95_size: 12
  p99_size: 34

observed: microbatches occasionally coalesce into a large tail (>> configured max) when seq_len variance high
```

ben: That cb profile shows KV misses are amplifying tail. We should consider: 1) pre-emptive truncation for huge prompts 2) cap microbatch by token budget not just request count 3) faster fallback kernel for long-seqs.
miro: +1. Also saw a kernel selection regression in last runtime deploy where we preferred FP16 matmul that degraded long-seq throughput. Reverting gives better p99 but slightly worse median. Tradeoff.
omar: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- enforce per-request max_prompt_tokens and max_generated_tokens at router (hard cap)
- implement token-budgeted microbatching: microbatch_token_cap = 4096 (sum of seq_len across requests)
- early KV eviction heuristic: prefer "cold-evict" for keys older than 30m during congestion
- tail-timeout: if a microbatch doesn't make progress for 800ms, preempt and fallback to smaller kernel

sangeeta: Will these be config flags? can you draft the runtime defaults?
ben: Draft snippet:

```
service_defaults:
  slo:
    p95_ms: "120"
    p99_ms: "420"
  batching:
    max_microbatch_count: 16
    microbatch_token_cap: 4096
    token_budget_mode: true
  timeouts:
    generation_timeout_ms: 30000
    tail_detection_ms: 800
  truncation:
    policy: "left-truncate"
    max_prompt_tokens: 2048
    max_generated_tokens: 512
  kv_cache:
    eviction_policy: "age-aware-lru"
    cold_threshold_minutes: 30
    aggressive_eviction_on_congestion: true
```

miro: I want to tweak: for models with efficient long-kernel (e.g., kernel-v3-long), set microbatch_token_cap to 8192 and allow larger microbatch_count but with stricter tail_detection_ms (500ms). We need per-model profiles.
omar: Agree. Add model profiles map in config. Also a runtime experiment: if a request's seq_len > 4k, force dedicated single-request path (no batching) to avoid high-latency coalescing.
sangeeta: For truncation: prefer left-truncate for chats but preserve last N turns. Maybe implement a smart truncator that keeps message boundaries and a small summary token budget.
ben: Algorithm idea for smart truncator: keep last 3 turns fully, then summary block of earlier context capped at 512 tokens. Simple pseudo: 
```
if prompt_tokens > max_prompt_tokens:
  keep = last_turns(3)
  rest_summary = summarize(prefix)  # async, cached
  rebuilt_prompt = rest_summary + keep
```
miro: That summary step needs cached summaries per convo-id in KV to avoid compute cost. Ties back to KV cache design.

infra-bot: Deploy check: current rollout 0% -> can't change kernel selection without coordinator approval. Use feature flag `runtime_tail_safeguards` to toggle.
omar: Plan for next 48h:
- hotfix router caps + token-budgeted batching (ben) — target: roll to 10% in 2h, 100% in 6h if green
- enable aggressive KV eviction under congestion (sangeeta) — staged rollout alongside perf tests
- add model-profile overrides for microbatch_token_cap (miro) — collect perf runs
- add observability: per-microbatch token histogram + microbatch age gauge (ben)

sangeeta: I'll add regression tests that simulate high-seq variance and assert p99 < 2x baseline after mitigations.
ben: Quick command to repro locally (use perf harness):
```
./perf_runner --model redwood-long-v1 --clients 80 --seq_len_dist heavy_tail --duration 600 --collect-microbatch-stats
```
miro: For followups: need to evaluate effect of kernel fallback on cost. Median might increase but p99 drop could be worth it for SLO customers. Add cost telemetry per-route.
omar: Thanks. I'll open a short RFC with the config defaults and experiment plan. If anyone wants to pair on tests ping me. :thumbsup:
ben: pinged infra on the feature flag.
sangeeta: I'll start KV eviction PR now and wire the summary-caching plan.
miro: I'll run a couple of long-run perf experiments overnight and post results here tomorrow.
omar: Great — appreciate the quick sync.
